schemes.description: Annual week-long, non-credit project week for undergraduates. Students choose one themed Challenge (2026 themes include Climate and Environment Emergency, Defence Security and Resilience, Social Inequality, Education Innovation, Mental Health, and a Penryn planetary-health challenge), join an enquiry group and work in interdisciplinary groups of normally 4-8 to design solutions to a real-world problem, presenting to academic experts (Streatham) or a panel of independent experts (Penryn) at the end of the week, with a Forum showcase. Lectures are led by academics and external experts; for some challenges industry experts attend the presentations. No evidence that an external organisation sets the brief or receives/assesses outputs for the standard enquiry groups (the AWS industry-led group is recorded separately as S2).
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: All undergraduate programmes (Streatham and Penryn campuses; Penryn challenge Penryn-only)
schemes.year_of_study: Any undergraduate year (FAQ refers to enrolled undergraduates)
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Enrolled University of Exeter undergraduates; one Challenge per student; free as part of tuition
schemes.credit_assessment: No credit evidenced; final group presentation
schemes.delivery_format: In person, Streatham and Penryn campuses
schemes.project_evidence: Groups design innovative solutions to a defined real-world challenge and present ideas to an expert panel [1][2][3].
schemes.group_evidence: 'Groups vary in size, and normally contain 4 to 8 people' [1]; interdisciplinary groups [2].
schemes.employer_evidence: External involvement evidenced only as external-expert lectures, 'independent experts' on the Penryn panel and, for some challenges, industry experts in the audience [2][3]. No source shows external organisations setting briefs, acting as clients or assessing for the standard enquiry groups; external experts as speakers/audience do not satisfy C.
schemes.partner_role: External experts give lectures; independent experts sit on Penryn presentation panel; industry experts sometimes in the audience
schemes.deliverable: Group presentation of proposed solution (plus showcase)
schemes.unresolved: Whether any enquiry groups besides S2 have external organisations setting briefs; the Grand Challenges home page reportedly lists 7-11 June 2027, while challenge pages are under 'challenges2026' - the 2026 pages are taken as dated evidence of 2025/26 delivery. Participation numbers not found.

schemes.description: 12-week online programme run by Exeter with QS (Future17 consortium of 12 universities). After a 4-week induction, students spend 8 weeks in international, interdisciplinary teams (typically 6-8, drawn from at least two partner universities) working on a sustainability (SDG) challenge set by a Challenge Partner (business, charity, NGO), with an academic mentor; assessed on a group report (or equivalent) and an online group presentation to an expert panel including a representative of the challenge partner.
schemes.admin_host: Global Classrooms / Future17 team with QS
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: All programmes, all campuses (UG excluding first years; PGT)
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Undergraduates except first years, and postgraduate taught students, all campuses; once only per student; competitive limited places; credit route subject to available optional credit and programme rules
schemes.credit_assessment: Optional 15 credits at level 6 via APEL (module BEP3172) replacing an optional module, or non-credit route with QS certificate. Assessed on group project output and group presentation [1][3].
schemes.project_evidence: Teams address a defined partner-set sustainability challenge producing a report (or equivalent) and presentation [1][2].
schemes.group_evidence: Small groups of typically 6-8 students from at least two partner universities; group project output and group presentation [1].
schemes.employer_evidence: Challenge Partner outlines the challenge, provides context and potentially data; assessment panel includes a representative of the partner that set the challenge [1]; 31 organisations provided 44 challenges in a recent round [2].

schemes.deliverable: Group report (or equivalent) and online group presentation
schemes.participation_data: About 50 Exeter students graduated in the cohort reported (c.2024/25), c.300 worldwide [2]
schemes.unresolved: No dated 2025/26 or 2026/27 call/cohort found (search budget exhausted); module page is 2024/5; graduation news dated c. spring 2025 from search metadata. Attribution of partner-role text among Future17 pages not fully explicit. Exeter news refers to an 8th cohort (nearly 240 students since 2022) but date not confirmed in search; stays status unclear.

profile_md:
**Exeter** has two university-wide extracurricular routes. Embedded programme provision is mainly in the Business School. Review incomplete (search budget exhausted).

- **Grand Challenges** (legacy): a free June project week open to all undergraduates. Groups of normally 4-8 design solutions to themed real-world challenges and present them to expert panels. 2026 challenge pages confirm current delivery. External input is largely experts giving lectures or sitting in the audience, so C is Unclear. The exception is a 2026 *Industry-led Enquiry Group with Amazon Web Services*, but AWS's exact role was not evidenced.
- **Future17** (legacy, with QS): open to undergraduates in year 2 or later and to PGT students. International teams of 6-8 spend 12 weeks on challenges set by partner organisations; 31 organisations offered 44 challenges in one round. A partner representative sits on the assessment panel. It can be taken for 15 credits via APEL or without credit. It meets all three criteria, but the latest dated cohort is about 2024/25, so its status is unclear.
- **Business School:** the compulsory **BEMM149 Business Project** on MSc Management is a group consultancy project on a partner's brief, with a report and presentation for the partner. It meets A/B/C, but the page is undated. The other routes are incomplete:
  - BEMM771 (2018/19 only)
  - BEP3020 (live or simulated)
  - the MSc Marketing and Business Analytics consulting option (group format unknown)
  - the MBA capstone, which is individual
- **Engineering and Computing:** substantial group projects (ECMM102, ENEM010, ECM2434, ECMM427). Industry involvement is 'may' or unverified.
- **Science:** no qualifying route found. Green Consultants uses the University itself as client.
- **Uncertain:** no qualifying scheme with current delivery has been verified. Not yet checked: the AHSS modules, Law/Health, and dated evidence for Future17 and BEMM149.
gaps: Other area unsearched; AHSS barely searched; dated current evidence missing for Future17 and BEMM149; AWS role in Grand Challenges; ECMM427 customer; group format for BEP3020, MSc MBA consulting option, Sports Consultancy Project; One Planet MBA team challenges; further departmental instances likely (engineering, business MSc programmes). Medicine/Health, Psychology, Sport not separately searched; reduced-depth mode.
